short: These reins in Spain fight mainly on the plain.
history: The Iberian Peninsula was wealthy in many resources - iron and silver were natural minerals found in abundance there, but the region was also famous for breeding war horses at a time when cavalry warfare was becoming more popular once again. Islamic forces were augmented with highly-proficient Berber cavalry, whilst to the north the Franks under Charlemagne were fielding heavy, armoured riders in the style of the eastern cataphracts. The Frankish knights saw themselves as the right-hand of both their king and God, and fought with a brutal fervour to match the religious ideals of their Muslim enemies. The Asturians attempted to emulate Frankish ideals in this matter, fielding their own mounted knights to combat the Caliphate's growing army and return Spain to Christian hands.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
